acceptable_changes: Cut the optional bankrupt-the-world calculation and the Texan/lantern-fish joke together, along with the later deep-sea-fish restatement, so no orphaned fish reference remains.
Removed the Polish Jew comparison sentence and the Europe/Asia polarization clause from paragraph 2 to compress it, while keeping the self-exculpation irony intact.
Dropped the Boston two-o'clock dinner and Back Bay skating details, and cut the State Street office and elevator fantasy as a whole.
Compressed the Tribune, Sun and Herald detail to roughly one sentence each and cut the Whitelaw Reid aside.
Cut the sleeping-car aside but kept the shelter of Evarts's house.
Reduced the list of volunteer names to Frank Walker alone, and trimmed the reform, finance and tariff discussion.
Cut the village tram, Mullett asylum, real-estate and Jackson monument details, the Sam Ward lobby aside, and the Conkling comparison.
Shortened the Sumner rupture passage to a brief reference to the already-known eight years of broken ties.
review_focus: Transition from Seward's whist dinner to McCulloch: check that the friend-in-power rule and McCulloch's exception remain intact.
Chase sentence: check that he is the author of Legal Tender as Secretary and its enemy as Chief Justice.
Desbrosses Street references after the North River pier landing: both appear in the source.
Check that Grant's cabinet and the omitted chapters' material are not mentioned.
risks: Total length has not been measured and may run somewhat under 3300 words because most retained sentences are kept close to source wording.
The section on Johnson, Seward, McCulloch and the reformers is the longest and may exceed its 660-word allocation, while the press section runs shorter.
summary: Abridgment of 'The Press (1868)' that keeps the landing with Motley, the caravan and earthworm images, bric-a-brac, the railway mortgage, the Charles/Henry division, Boston, Newport and the departure, the press survey, Evarts, Johnson, Seward, McCulloch and the friend-in-power rule, the Evarts anvil and Chase's Legal Tender irony, Sumner, the village, and the closing verdict. All eight verbatim excerpts are retained exactly.
